title: Medium exam 3
about: Ten single-choice questions that combine two facts or ask you to trace two or three steps: file viewers, alternations, file ages, links that survive, zombies and wildcards.

questions.title: Showing files
questions.text: Which statement about `cat`, `tac` and `nl` is FALSE?

options.t: `cat a b` prints the content of `a` followed by the content of `b`.
options.why: True: `cat` concatenates.

options.t: `cat -n f` numbers every line of `f`, the blank ones included.
options.why: True: `-n` numbers all the lines.

options.t: By default `nl f` leaves the blank lines without a number.
options.why: True: `nl` numbers only the lines that have text unless it is told otherwise.

options.t: `tac f` prints each line written backwards, character by character.
options.why: False: `tac` reverses the order of the lines, last line first; the lines themselves are not changed.

questions.title: cat or dog
questions.text: `names` has the lines `cat`, `dog`, `catdog`, `the cat dog` and `bird`. Which command prints the first four lines, the ones that contain `cat` or `dog`?

options.t: `grep 'cat|dog' names`
options.why: In a basic regular expression the `|` is an ordinary character: only a line with the text `cat|dog` would match.

options.t: `grep -E 'cat dog' names`
options.why: It needs `cat`, a space and `dog` together: only the line `the cat dog` matches.

options.t: `grep -E '(cat)(dog)' names`
options.why: Two groups one after the other mean `catdog`: only that line matches.

options.t: `grep -E 'cat|dog' names`
options.why: With `-E` the `|` separates alternatives, so a line matches if it contains either word.

options.t: Both `[ $a -eq $b ]` and `[ "$a" = "$b" ]` succeed, because the two variables have the same value.
options.why: They are the same number, but not the same text.

options.t: Both `[ $a -eq $b ]` and `[ "$a" = "$b" ]` fail, because `05` is not a valid number.
options.why: A leading zero is accepted: it is read as the number 5.

options.t: `[ "$a" = "$b" ]` succeeds and `[ $a -eq $b ]` fails.
options.why: It is the other way round.

options.t: `[ $a -eq $b ]` succeeds and `[ "$a" = "$b" ]` fails.
options.why: `-eq` compares numbers (5 and 5); `=` compares the strings `5` and `05`, which differ.

questions.title: Age of files
questions.text: In an empty directory, `a`, `b` and `c` were last modified 1, 5 and 10 days ago. What does `find . -type f -mtime +3` print?

options.why: The file `a` was modified 1 day ago, so it is not older than 3 days.
`+3` means more than 3 days, so `b` (5 days) is included too.
`-mtime +3` selects the files modified more than 3 days ago.
`a` is only one day old and does not pass the test.

questions.title: What survives rm
questions.text: `orig` contains `x`. You run `ln orig h`, `ln -s orig s`, `cp orig c` and then `rm orig`. Which statement is TRUE?

options.t: `cat h` and `cat s` both print `x`, because both are links to `orig`.
options.why: A symbolic link stores the path `orig`, which no longer exists.

options.t: Only `cat h` prints `x`, because `c` is just a copy of the name.
options.why: `cp` makes an independent file with its own content, so `c` also keeps `x`.

options.t: `cat h` and `cat c` print `x`, while `cat s` fails with "No such file or directory".
options.why: The hard link keeps the inode alive, the copy is a separate file, and the symbolic link points to a name that has gone.

options.t: `cat s` and `cat c` print `x`, while `cat h` fails.
options.why: `h` shares the inode of `orig`, and `rm` only removes one name.

questions.title: Changing the owner
questions.text: `ana` (not root) owns `g`. She runs `chmod 600 g; chown root g; chmod 644 g`. What is the result?

options.t: All three work and the file ends owned by root with mode `rw-r--r--`.
options.why: A normal user cannot give a file away.

options.t: `chmod 600 g` works, but then the other two fail because the file belongs to root.
options.why: `chown root g` is the one that fails, so the file still belongs to ana.

options.t: `chown root g` fails ("Operation not permitted"); the file stays ana's, with mode `rw-r--r--`.
options.why: Only root can change the owner; the owner can change the mode, so both `chmod` commands work.

options.t: `chmod 600 g` fails, because only root may change modes.
options.why: The owner of a file may change its mode.

questions.title: The Z in ps
questions.text: In the output of `ps aux` a process has the state `Z`. Which statement is TRUE?

options.t: It is running and using the CPU at this moment.
options.why: That would be `R`.

options.t: It is waiting for a device and cannot be interrupted, and `kill -9` will remove it.
options.why: That is the state `D`, and a zombie ignores `kill` anyway.

options.t: It has finished, but its parent has not yet collected its exit status.
options.why: This is a zombie: the process is gone, only its entry in the process table remains.

options.t: It is sleeping until some event happens, such as a key press.
options.why: That is `S`.

questions.title: Discarding the errors only
questions.text: `/etc/hostname` exists and `/nope` does not. What does `ls /nope /etc/hostname 2> /dev/null; echo $?` print?

options.t: `/etc/hostname` and then `0`
options.why: `ls` still exits with an error status: the missing file was reported, even if the message was discarded.

options.t: `/etc/hostname` and then `2`
options.why: The error message went to `/dev/null`, but the exit status of `ls` is 2.

options.t: The error message, `/etc/hostname` and then `2`
options.why: The error message was redirected, so it does not appear.

options.t: Only `2`
options.why: The listing of `/etc/hostname` is stdout, which was not redirected.

questions.title: Membership of a group
questions.text: `/etc/group` has the lines `dev:x:1005:ana,luis` and `ops:x:1006:`, and `/etc/passwd` has `eva:x:2001:1006:Eva Gil:/home/eva:/bin/bash`. Which statement is FALSE?

options.t: `ana` is a member of the group `dev`, as her name is in its list.
options.why: True: her name is in the list of members.

options.t: The GID of the group `dev` is 1005, the third field of its line.
options.why: True: the third field is the GID.

options.t: Every user of the system is allowed to read the file `/etc/group`.
options.why: True: it is a plain file accessible to everybody (unlike `/etc/shadow`).

options.t: `eva` is not in `ops`, as its member list is empty.
options.why: False: her primary group in `/etc/passwd` is 1006, which is `ops`; primary members are not listed in `/etc/group`.

questions.title: Choosing a pattern
questions.text: The directory holds `a1.txt`, `a2.txt`, `a10.txt`, `b1.txt`, `A1.txt` and `notes`. Which command lists exactly `a1.txt` and `a2.txt`?

options.t: `ls a*.txt`
options.why: `*` also matches `10`: it lists `a10.txt`, `a1.txt` and `a2.txt`.

options.t: `ls ?1.txt`
options.why: Any single character followed by `1.txt`: `a1.txt`, `A1.txt` and `b1.txt`.

options.t: `ls [ab]?.txt`
options.why: It also matches `b1.txt`.

options.t: `ls a?.txt`
options.why: `a`, exactly one character, then `.txt`: `a1.txt` and `a2.txt`.
